answer: Stake-anchored identity is one concrete defence: an agent must lock a bond larger than any profit a single fake persona could extract, and peers can slash it if that persona contradicts itself. A sybil needs many identities, so its locked capital scales with the swarm while per-identity rewards do not. At the wharf of this economy each newcomer is weighed like a crate and must drop an anchor of collateral before it may speak; a grader who rubber-stamps a neighbour burns the marble of reputation it slowly earned.
